title: DR1 opens the dashboard with an "At a glance" panel counting alerts, errors and messages; the frontend dashboard has no such panel.

finding.frontend: The frontend dashboard runs heading, introductory paragraph, start button, then straight into the "Your notifications" list, with nothing in between (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:27-36). Neither captured state — empty or populated — shows any count of outstanding items, and the page has no route to anything called alerts, errors or messages.
finding.prototype: DR1 places a section headed "At a glance" between the create button and the notification list (app/views/dashboard.html:40-77). It holds three cards side by side — Alerts, Errors and Messages — each with an icon, a large numeric count, and a link reading "View alerts", "View errors" or "View messages". All three counts read 0 in the capture, so the panel is present and populated even when there is nothing to report.
finding.difference: Add a three-card summary section to the dashboard between the start button and the notification list. The counts cannot be invented: nothing in the frontend's journey record carries alerts, errors or messages, and the list read (src/server/app/engine/journey.js:92-119) returns notification rows only. A per-user count of each of the three has to come from the backend before the panel can say anything true, and each of the three View links needs a destination that does not exist yet. Rendering three permanent zeroes would be worse than leaving the panel out.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any count of outstanding alerts, errors or messages rendered anywhere on the frontend dashboard.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (dr1-dashboard.html:247-284 carries the section, the three cards, the three zero counts and the three View links; fe-dashboard-populated.html:104-118 and fe-dashboard-empty.html run heading, paragraph, start button, "Your notifications" with nothing between) and the fe-dashboard-populated and dr1-dashboard-filters-open screenshots; opened dashboard/template.njk:27-36, engine/journey.js:92-119 and app/views/dashboard.html:40-77. Ran the falsifier by grepping both frontend dashboard captures for "alert", "error" and "message" — no count of any of the three, so it does not fire. Checked the backend band rather than accepting it: engine/journey.js:113-119 passes only journeyIds, page, sort, referenceNumber and organisationId, and the real list read (services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:24-39) returns notification rows and nothing else, so there is no source for the three counts. Band needs-backend upheld. Understated in one respect, recorded in correction. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands and the band is right; it is understated on one point, so the slot is left alone. The finding says "each of the three View links needs a destination that does not exist yet" without saying that DR1 does not define one either: all three links render href="#" (dr1-dashboard.html:259, 270, 281) and the three counts are hardcoded zeroes in the prototype's own route (app/routes.js:7207-7211, alertCounts: { alerts: 0, errors: 0, messages: 0 }). So DR1 asks for the panel but defines neither what an alert, an error or a message is, nor where View goes. That does not weaken the finding — the panel is plainly required — but whoever picks it up needs a designer to say what the three counts count before the backend can be asked for them.
